goal: Implement seal(code) and is_sealed(text) in rune_seal.py: seal normalises a rune code and appends '-' and a check character computed with cycling weights 1, 3, 7, an echo rule and the code length modulo 28; is_sealed tells whether a text ends in its correct check character.
behaviors: seal("5") returns "5-6" (the check value is the weighted sum plus the number of characters, modulo 28).
seal("56") returns "56-W" and seal("567") returns "567-M" (weights cycle 1, 3, 7 from the left; values above 9 map to letters of the alphabet).
seal("55") returns "55-7" (a character equal to the one before it contributes nothing).
seal("c-d e") returns "CDE-1" (lowercase letters are uppercased, hyphens and spaces removed).
seal("O") and seal("") each raise ValueError.
is_sealed("56-W") returns True, while is_sealed("56-X") and is_sealed("5") return False.

assumptions.text: rune_seal.py exists at the repo root as the single flat module.
The tests/ directory exists for the new test file.
pyproject.toml exists so the project toolchain is configured.
pytest can be run through uv without network access.

demo: python -c 'from rune_seal import seal, is_sealed; print(seal("ac 77")); print(is_sealed("ac77d"))'
out_of_scope: Unicode case folding beyond ASCII a-z

invariants.text: a sealed code is the normal form, a hyphen and one check character
the check character is in the rune alphabet
